items.title: 68087_Cliff Leeman oral history interview
items.q: when I was with the Peanuts Hucko Quartet... Peanuts had been with Louis for a long time... Afterwards, he had Lou McGarity and Peanuts and myself over to his table

ctx.x: And when we got there, he had his right hand man put on a bunch of records, and we settled back and listened to Louis, and he played nothing but Bobby Hackett records. Well, we sort of hinted that we'd like to hear some of his records.

Then when I was with the Peanuts Hucko Quartet at the Roosevelt Grill, Louis had been real sick towards the end, and he was recuperating. He came down with his wife, Lucille, to hear us. Peanuts had been with Louis for a long time -- he did some of those lengthy world wide trips with him. He made some movies with him, and that was a few years back, and Louis got up for nostalgia's sake, I couldn't believe it -- and he was a little bit weak, but he had that beautiful grin, and he came up on the bandstand and sang…

Afterwards, he had Lou McGarity and Peanuts and myself over to his table and he said, "Lucille, by my judge and witness; when I reorganize and I get to feel better, I want these three boys in my band" -- and he says,

items.title: 68087_Cliff Leeman oral history interview
items.q: We had Peanuts Hucko for a leader -- we were what you called the intermission band... The group the first two years was Ed Hubble on trombone, Peanuts Hucko on clarinet...

ctx.x: He continued his studies on drums, and along the way, after he went with Louis Armstrong -- he went all over the world with Louie Armstrong, and was such an outstanding soloist, and to this day, he's such a beautiful man, and he's still in the picture, I don't dare estimate what his age is -- I know it's around 70, and he's all over the world with Cootie Williams' orchestra, a small group, and they cover concerts all over the world, and they do some of the nicest work, and Cozy is still in there pitching. He is…

I must mention -- I did the first year of the Newport Festivals were starting, with Eddie Condon, for George Wein, Schroeder he was the promoter. We had Peanuts Hucko, Jack Lesberg, Gene Shrader, and Cutty Cutshall among others. And it rained

and it poured, and this great outdoor auditorium, and if you know anything about Eddie Condon, instead of playing the guitar, he took it upon himself to conduct the six pieces, and because of the rain which didn't cover the back, or the front of the show, where he announced, he had an umbrella over his head -- and it made quite a picture.
